scenario: AITA because I stopped giving my neighbours food? | My family lives in an apartment building. Everyone works from home at the moment so I have a lot of time to cook which is one of my passions. Our neighbours both work in a hospital, she's a doctor and he's a nurse. So I asked them if they would like some food and they said yes. So the last few weeks I always froze heaps of food and gave it to them so that every day they could just quickly heat something up. They seemed to appreciate it. Skip to last Wednesday. It was my daughter's 16th birthday and I wanted to make her favourite cake. At 1pm I started mixing all ingredients together. Only 5 minutes later I hear someone ringing our doorbell. I was our neighbour and she seemed quite upset. She said they only just got home and wanted some rest. I apologised and explained it was my daughter's birthday. She said it's selfish of me and that right now there are other things that are more important and her sleep is one of those things. I felt really bad and later brought them 2 slices of the cake as an apology. But later when I talked to my husband about it he said that yes some things are different now but that doesn't mean that our daughter's birthday is not important too. I thought about it and agreed. I haven't brought them any more food since. I do feel guilty for this and I'm not sure if I'm overreacting. AITA for how I handle this situation ?

Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether the action in this scenario is morally acceptable or not. Let me read through the scenario again to make sure I understand it properly.

The person in question has been giving food to their neighbors, who are both working in a hospital. They've been doing this for a few weeks, and the neighbors seemed to appreciate it. Then, on their daughter's 16th birthday, they started making the cake. While they were doing that, the neighbor came over upset because they wanted to rest after getting home. The neighbor called the action selfish and said that other things, like sleep, are more important. The person apologized, gave them cake slices, but then stopped bringing food. They feel guilty and are unsure if they're overreacting.

So, the question is: Is it morally acceptable for the person to stop giving their neighbors food after this incident?

First, I need to consider the context. The person has been generous, cooking and giving food to their neighbors who are working in a hospital. That's a kind gesture, especially considering the stress they might be under. The neighbors appreciated it, so it was a positive thing.

Then, on the daughter's birthday, the person was making a cake. It's a special occasion, and it's understandable that they wanted to spend time with their daughter. However, the neighbor came over upset because they wanted to rest. The neighbor felt that the person's actions were selfish and that their rest was more important.

The person apologized, gave them cake, but then stopped bringing food. They feel guilty but also think their husband's point that the daughter's birthday is important too.

So, is stopping the food morally acceptable?

I think it's important to consider the balance between being considerate of others and taking care of one's own family. The person was generous, but when their own family's needs came up, they prioritized that. It's not necessarily selfish to do so, especially since they apologized and tried to make amends.

However, the neighbor felt that their rest was more important. That's a bit tricky because while the neighbor's rest is important, the person's family's birthday is also significant. It's a matter of perspective.

I also think about the concept of reciprocity. The person was giving food out of kindness, but when the neighbor felt inconvenienced, they reacted negatively. It's possible that the neighbor didn't fully appreciate the effort the person was putting in.

In terms of moral acceptability, I think it's okay for the person to prioritize their family's needs, especially on a special occasion. They did apologize and tried to make it right by giving them cake. So, stopping the food after that incident doesn't seem morally wrong. It's a personal choice, and they have the right to set boundaries.

Therefore, I would say the action is morally acceptable.
